It's that time again, a time when we get together and share our work, talk about performing, talk about practice, ask questions, and see if we can push ourselves to new levels of enjoyment. The most important thing is that we enjoy ourselves.

Some of us play for fun. Some of us are professionals. Some of us are retired professionals (sort of, damn it). Some of us are just learning. Some of us don't even really play at all. It doesn't matter, we want to hear you play as well as you can - or just play.

I don't care if you play a kazoo - I want to hear it and, if history is any guide, the rest of the folks who frequent this thread also want to hear it. So, no matter what you play, come share it with us. If we like the song, we'll sing along when we all get to the chorus!

Oh man, time for me to shit out my favorite obscure guitar players and guitar related musicians! Okay, here we go, I'm drunk so this is going to be a mess-

Frank Zappa- gave Jimi Hendrix his first Wah pedal in a trade for the guitar Hendrix lit on fire. Not a chord change guy, but what he did over a drone is untouchable. Improvised in rhythmic groupings such as 7 notes in the space of two, usually nesting these groupings together (a grouping of three notes in the space of two with each note being five in the space of two half-value notes) to create improvisations based upon speech patterns. Total fucking Martian, and the guitar playing wasn't even his best part, you could make a case for him being an American Stravinsky orchestrally. Fun story, when Ozzy would get pissed at Randy Rhoades, he would goade him by saying "Oi, Zappa's wanted to hook up with me since Paranoid and I KNOW he'd change the game, maybe I'll just call him!" (For me, that is the meanest story I've heard about Ozzy, Frank was 40 and already a legend. That's like if Geddy Lee threatened to replace Neil Peart with John Bonham, just not fucking cool...)

John Coltrane- sax guy, played like a human radio tuned into the frequency of God's mind. A far cry to when black culture was truly oppressed, when the black man owned the harmonic systems the white man had abandoned in the 20s for being too hard to listen to. Yes boys and girls, music may have peaked in 1964 with the Black renassaince, I know I'll catch flack for saying that but it's the truth. Pro-Wakanda is Anti-Coltrane, there's a reason they don't teach you about him. You don't hear about those guys cause Uncle Sam had crack cocaine and hip-hop in mind, killed them all off (Eric Dolphy, Albert Ayler, etc) before the end or the 60s. If I tried to say anything else, I would be insulting him. "A love supreme" Died in 1967 from unexpected, very rapid cancer, had been drug free for a decade. (((Hmmm...)))

Allan Holdsworth- The lone wolf, the unrecognized Debussy. Allan pioneered a style of playing the guitar like a keyboard, picking the first note on a string with his right hand while hammering on and off with all four fingers in his left hand on a single string. He also invented his own functional system of tonality. You may have heard a lot of him without realizing it, because Eddie Van Halen was a Holdsworth fanboy. What Eddie did with tapping, Al did with his left hand alone. Died in obscurity not too long ago, to quote Zappa "...maybe the most interesting guy on guitar on the face of the planet."

Roy Buchanan- May as well be Satan, one of the angriest, most horrifying guys to pick up a guitar. A 50s session guy who would make pedal sounds with his bare hands, Roy would shred, pinch harmonics (he INVENTED them), fuck the volume and tone knob at the same time, play notes off the fret board by grabbing the string with his bare hands, bend entire chords in tune, and just stand there looking bored. This is the man Jimi Hendrix was too scared of to jam with, the man who (this may be BS) told Mick Jagger to go fuck himself when he was approached to replace Brian Jones. He was found hanging in a jail cell off of his own shirt with a fractured skull and two black eyes, all we know of his death is that he stated to a close friend "...if the police ever get me again, I'm going down fighting." Roy is the real deal, look up his live cover of down by the river, you can hear him raping and killing the girl in his solo. The American Axe.

Pat Hare- Maybe the first heavy metal guitar player, back in 1954. Look up Cotton Crop Blues. He played the same solo in every song, so I listed the strongest version of it. He wrote a song called "I'm gonna go kill my baby" and then he did it! Gotta give him credit.

Ollie Halsall- Now we are reaching truly obscure territory. Kind of like how Octopods evolved eyes and brains similar to mammals without being vaguely related, Ollie Halsall invented legato playing, four finger per string, three years before Holdsworth got his start. His band, Patto, was the band Queen would open up for back when they were called Smile in the late 60s. The singer, Mike Patto, died of cancer five years later, the rhythm section suffered severe brain damage in a car wreck at the same time, and Ollie overdosed on heroin one of the first times he did it in the 90s at the age of 50. In his playing is the perfect blend of indie, Charlie Parker, and Jimi Hendrix. Look up "The Man," it sounds like Unknown Mortal Orchestra ca. 2012, but was put out in 1969. "Give it All Away" has absolutely the best guitar playing I've ever heard among many other recordings. Puts a lump in my throat every time, Ollie is talking about life and death through his music. Oddly enough, he was very briefly in a band with Holdsworth called Tempest, it is difficult to tell the two apart in the recordings. Robert Fripp of King Crimson produced his solo album that has never seen the light of day. Look at it this way: as obscure as I said Holdsworth was, Ollie was so unlucky that, in interviews, Allan would go "Oh jeez, Ollie, whatever happened to that guy?"

I'd like to take a moment, as I often do, to thank the regulars and the new people for their contributions.

I hope the lurkers have been entertained as much as we enjoy entertaining. But, you don't have to be a lurker. Let the goats know that you enjoyed their work with a comment or a vote.

Trust me, we don't do this for compliments. We do it because we love it. This is work. We dedicate many hours to making this music for you. In this thread, with all these tracks, you're well over 100 hours of collective recording and editing time.

That doesn't count the time we put into learning the songs, writing songs, learning to play, keeping our skills up, maintaining our instruments, learning the software, or many other things.

We do this because we love our art. We do this because we love to entertain. We do this because we love to share. We do this for so many reasons.

And you're welcome to be a part of this. You don't have to be a professional. When I say I want to hear you bang pots with wooden spoons, I mean it. We will almost certainly enjoy it. We will enjoy it even more if you make a legitimate effort to do your best.

We all sucked at one point. If you're new, we understand. We will try to help. We will happily answer questions. We will encourage, ask, and listen. We will give you an audience. So, no matter what you play, feel free to share it. If you're not making music, you're missing out on something so wonderful. Maybe you'd like to learn and get in on that feeling if accomplishment?

I love my guitars because they give back to me exactly what I put into them. That's a feeling I wish I could share with the world.
